config.title: transform: translate, scale, rotate

intro.title: transform: translate, scale, rotate
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple interactive card that moves, changes size, and spins when you hover over it. You will learn the core concept of CSS transforms, which allow you to modify the position, scale, and rotation of HTML elements. The main technologies involved are the CSS transform property and its functions: translate(), scale(), and rotate(). This will help you create engaging visual effects without changing the document's layout. By the end, you'll be able to apply these transformations to any element on a webpage.
intro.usecase: The transform property is essential for creating interactive UI components that respond to user actions. You'll use translate() to slide elements like modals into view or create animated navigation menus. Scale() is perfect for zooming product images on hover in e-commerce sites or highlighting interactive buttons. Rotate() adds polish to loading spinners, toggle switches, and directional indicators in dashboards and mobile apps.

objectives: Apply the transform property to HTML elements using CSS
Configure translate values to reposition elements along the X and Y axes
Manipulate element size by implementing scale transformations
Control element rotation by applying rotate with degree units
Integrate multiple transform functions in a single declaration
Construct interactive effects by combining transform with pseudo-classes

steps.title: Create a basic HTML structure with a target element
steps.instruction: Create a simple HTML structure with a div element that will serve as our transformation target. Use a class name 'box' for the div.
steps.hint: Start with a basic HTML structure. Add a div element with the class attribute set to 'box'.
steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <title>CSS Transform Demo</title>
</head>
<body>
    <!-- Add your target div here -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: The HTML file will have a div element with class 'box' that we can later style and transform.
successCriteria: The HTML contains a div element with class='box' inside the body.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a div element with class='box' inside the body.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a simple HTML structure with a div element that has class='box'.

steps.title: Add base styling to the target element
steps.instruction: Add a <style> block inside the <head> section to create a visible target element with width: 200px, height: 200px, and background-color: #3498db.
steps.hint: Inside the <head> section, add <style> tags and define a CSS rule for a class like .target-element with the specified properties.
steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <title>CSS Transform Demo</title>
    <!-- Add your style block here -->
</head>
<body>
    <!-- Add your target div here -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: A style block is added to the HTML head, defining a target element with basic dimensions and color.
successCriteria: The <head> contains a <style> block with a CSS rule defining width: 200px, height: 200px, and background-color: #3498db.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some styling, but ensure you include all three properties: width: 200px, height: 200px, and background-color: #3498db.
steps.feedbackWrong: The style block is missing or incomplete. Add a <style> block in the <head> with a CSS rule for the target element.

steps.title: Introduce the transform property
steps.instruction: Add a style block to the head section and apply the transform property with a value of 'none' to the target element.
steps.hint: Use the <style> tag inside the <head> section. Target the div element and set transform: none;
steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <title>CSS Transform Demo</title>
    <!-- Add your style block here -->
</head>
<body>
    <!-- Add your target div here -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: The HTML document will have a style block in the head section with a CSS rule that applies transform: none; to a div element.
successCriteria: A style block is added to the head section with a CSS rule targeting a div element and setting transform: none;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added a style block in the head section and applied transform: none; to a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The transform property hasn't been correctly introduced. Check that you've added a style block and applied transform: none; to a div element.

steps.title: Apply translate transformation
steps.instruction: Inside the style block, add a transform property with translate(50px, 30px) to the .box rule to move it horizontally and vertically.
steps.hint: The translate function takes two values: horizontal (X) and vertical (Y) movement. Positive values move right/down.
steps.expectedOutcome: The blue square will move 50 pixels to the right and 30 pixels down from its original position.
successCriteria: The .box selector has transform: translate(50px, 30px); applied.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're adding transform: translate(50px, 30px); inside the .box rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The translate transformation wasn't applied correctly. Check that you're using the correct syntax: transform: translate(50px, 30px);

steps.title: Experiment with translateX and translateY separately
steps.instruction: In the .box CSS rule, replace the comment with a transform property that uses translateX to move the box 50px to the right.
steps.hint: Use transform: translateX(50px); to move the element horizontally. This will replace the comment placeholder.
steps.analogousExample:
/* Similar: moving an element horizontally */
transform: translateX(30px);
steps.expectedOutcome: The blue box will shift 50 pixels to the right from its original position.
successCriteria: The .box CSS rule contains transform: translateX(50px);
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using transform: translateX(50px); exactly as specified to move the box to the right.
steps.feedbackWrong: The transform property should be translateX(50px) to move the box horizontally. Check your syntax.

steps.title: Introduce scale transformation
steps.instruction: In the .box CSS rule, replace the translate transformation with a scale transformation to make the element larger.
steps.hint: Use the transform property with the scale() function. Try scale(1.5) to enlarge the box by 50%.
steps.expectedOutcome: The blue box should appear larger than its original size, positioned where it was before (no translation).
successCriteria: The .box rule includes transform: scale() with a value greater than 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the scale() function inside transform, and remove the translate() function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you replaced the translate transformation with scale. The transform property should only contain scale().

steps.title: Experiment with scaleX and scaleY separately
steps.instruction: In the .box CSS rule, replace the current transform property with scaleX(1.5) to stretch the element horizontally.
steps.hint: The scaleX function scales an element along the horizontal axis. Use transform: scaleX(1.5); to make the box 1.5 times wider.
steps.expectedOutcome: The blue box will appear stretched horizontally while maintaining its vertical height and translated position.
successCriteria: The .box CSS rule contains transform: scaleX(1.5);
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using scaleX(1.5) and removing the translate property.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've replaced the transform property with scaleX(1.5) in the .box rule.

steps.title: Introduce rotate transformation
steps.instruction: In the .box CSS rule, replace the transform property value with rotate(45deg) to spin the element 45 degrees clockwise.
steps.hint: The rotate() function takes an angle value (like 45deg). Replace the existing translate() value with rotate(45deg).
steps.expectedOutcome: The blue square will rotate 45 degrees clockwise from its original position instead of being translated.
successCriteria: The .box rule's transform property is set to rotate(45deg).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the rotate() function with an angle value like 45deg.
steps.feedbackWrong: The rotation wasn't applied correctly. Check that you replaced the transform value with rotate(45deg).

steps.title: Combine translate and rotate transformations
steps.instruction: In the .box CSS rule, modify the transform property to combine both translate and rotate transformations.
steps.hint: You can apply multiple transformations by listing them in order within the same transform property, separated by spaces.
steps.expectedOutcome: The blue box will be moved 20px right and 20px down, then rotated by 45 degrees clockwise.
successCriteria: The .box rule includes a transform property with both translate and rotate functions in sequence.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you have both translate and rotate functions in the transform property, separated by a space.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've modified the transform property to include both translate and rotate functions in the correct order.

steps.title: Combine translate, scale, and rotate transformations
steps.instruction: In the .box CSS rule, add scale(1.5) and rotate(45deg) to the existing transform property, separating them with a space.
steps.hint: Multiple transform functions can be chained in a single transform property by listing them in order with spaces between.
steps.expectedOutcome: The blue box will be moved 20px right and down, scaled 1.5 times larger, and rotated 45 degrees clockwise.
successCriteria: The .box CSS rule contains transform: translate(20px, 20px) scale(1.5) rotate(45deg);
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added both scale(1.5) and rotate(45deg) to the existing transform property, separated by spaces.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've modified the transform property in the .box rule to include translate(20px, 20px), scale(1.5), and rotate(45deg).

steps.title: Experiment with transformation order
steps.instruction: In the .box CSS rule, change the order of the transform functions to scale first,
steps.hint: The transform property can take multiple functions in a space-separated list. The order matters because each transformation builds on the previous one.
steps.expectedOutcome: The blue box will appear larger, rotated, and moved to a different position than before due to the changed transformation order.
successCriteria: The .box selector has a transform property with scale, rotate, and translate functions in that order.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have all three transform functions (scale, rotate, translate) in the correct order: scale first, then rotate, then translate.
steps.feedbackWrong: modify the transform property to include scale, rotate, and translate functions in that specific order.

steps.title: Add transition for smooth transformations
steps.instruction: Add a CSS transition property to the .box class to create smooth animation when transformations change.
steps.hint: Use the transition property with transform as the property to animate. You can set a duration like 0.3s.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .box element will smoothly animate when its transform property changes, making transformations appear fluid.
successCriteria: The .box class includes a transition property that targets transform with a specified duration.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added a transition property that targets the transform property with a duration.
steps.feedbackWrong: The transition property is missing or incorrect. Try adding 'transition: transform 0.3s ease;' to the .box class.
